venue.name: St. Ann's Academy National Historic Site
venue.description: St. Ann's Academy is a national historic site on Humboldt Street in Victoria, three blocks from the Inner Harbour, owned by the province through the Ministry of Citizens' Services. It was a Catholic girls' school and convent run by the Sisters of St. Ann until the school closed in 1973, and the province restored it between 1995 and 1997. The parts open to the public are the Interpretive Centre, the 1858 chapel with its ornate carvings and 1913 Casavant pipe organ, the parlours and foyer, and the heritage gardens and grounds. It is still open to visitors, with staff or volunteer docents on hand during opening hours, and it runs a free school program for BC classes.

facility_notes.lunch_space: Areas for eating lunch are available on request.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The main way in is up the grand double staircase. An alternative entrance with an elevator can be arranged, but you have to call ahead or send someone who can manage the stairs to tell the volunteer on duty, because the elevator door is kept locked.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Buses should park on the street.

The former classrooms and dormitories no longer exist, so the only historic interiors open are the parlours, foyer, chapel and former Priest's Breakfast Room
venue.hours_notes: The Interpretive Centre and Chapel are open Saturday and Sunday from 1:00pm to 4:00pm. Weekday site visits can be arranged by calling the office cell on 250-883-1824, which is answered Wednesday to Sunday. The outside grounds are open dawn to dusk. Phone ahead, because a wedding or other rental can close the inside at short notice.
venue.seasonal_notes: The school program runs September through June. The site hosts over 120 wedding rentals plus festivals and events each year, and those can restrict access, particularly in summer and holiday seasons.

programs.name: A Place in History
programs.description: A 90 minute school program offered free of charge to BC schools, recommended for Grades 2 and 3 and adaptable for Kindergarten to Grade 5. Advance booking is required. After a short orientation in the chapel the class splits into two groups and rotates through activity stations of about 15 minutes each, with a St. Ann's facilitator at every station. The three activities are a wood graining paint activity about how the building was made and restored, a session on Chinook trading phrases and archival photographs of early Victoria, and an outdoor mapping exercise on the grounds. A pre-visit booklet with photos, information and suggested classroom activities is sent to the teacher when the booking is made.
programs.what_children_do: Sit for a short welcome in the restored 1858 chapel, then split into two groups and move between three stations. They paint a wood graining pattern with poster paint after looking at the woodwork in the chapel and foyer, try saying phrases in Chinook and compare archival photographs of Victoria with the city now, and go outside to draw a map of the grounds and walk among the heritage trees and gardens.
programs.our_note: It is free and the facilitators run every station, so you are not left improvising. One activity is outdoors and one uses poster paint, so send the children in clothes that can take both. There is a cloakroom for coats and packs, and they will set aside somewhere to eat lunch if you ask for it when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are inside and somewhere to eat lunch can be arranged on request. There is a lift as an alternative to the grand staircase but it has to be arranged in advance, and buses have to park on the street rather than on site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Parking on the property is pay parking. If you book an appointment with the Interpretive Centre you may be able to arrange free parking for the length of the appointment, so ask staff.
programs.evidence: Description of Program Recommended for: Grades 2-3, adaptable for Grades K - 5.

programs.name: Customized group tour
programs.description: A staffed guided tour for groups, booked in advance, lasting about an hour. A donation of $5.00 per person is required. Groups need to be 10 or more and no larger than 30. The length and the subject can be changed to suit you, with topics including general history, architecture, art, religious studies, ghostly phenomena, and the gardens and grounds. Tours are also available in French, and visits outside normal opening hours can be arranged.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide through the restored parlours, the foyer and the 1858 chapel with its carved altar, gold leaf detailing, stained glass and pipe organ, then out into the Novitiate garden with its geometric herb bed and recreated 1925 summerhouse and the 1910 formal garden.
programs.our_note: This one is guided and mostly about looking rather than doing, so it suits a group that is already comfortable staying with a guide for an hour. The $5 is per person, not per group, so a class of 25 comes to $125 before you count adults. Ask what the topic will be when you book, because they will shape it around what you want.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are inside and lunch space can be arranged on request. There is a lift as an alternative to the grand staircase if you arrange it ahead, and buses park on the street.
programs.extra_fees_note: Parking on the property is pay parking.
programs.evidence: Group tours are available with advance booking. A donation of $5.00 per person is required.

programs.name: Self-guided visit
programs.description: During regular opening hours, and when no special event is booked, visitors can walk the Interpretive Centre and grounds on their own. A self-guided tour booklet is handed out at the Interpretive Centre in English, French, Spanish, Italian, German and Japanese, and can also be downloaded from the site, along with a botanical guide to the grounds. The booklet carries historic information plus recollections from former students, Sisters of St. Ann and heritage experts. Staff or volunteer docents are on hand to answer questions. What a visitor pays is not consistent across their pages, so ask at the door.
programs.what_children_do: Walk themselves through the parlours, foyer and chapel with a booklet, looking at the carved altar and ceiling, the stained glass and the pipe organ, then go out to the Novitiate garden, the summerhouse, the orchard and the heritage trees on the grounds.
programs.our_note: The public opening is only Saturday and Sunday afternoons, which rules it out for most weekday groups, though weekday site visits can be arranged by phone. Everything is behind rope or in a case, so it is looking rather than touching. Phone before you set out, because a wedding or a film shoot can shut the inside with no warning.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are inside and the grounds are open dawn to dusk. The way in is up a grand staircase unless you arrange the lift ahead, and buses park on the street rather than on site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Parking on the property is pay parking.
programs.evidence: visitors are welcome to explore the Interpretive Centre and grounds on a self-guided tour
